Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NovaRetail Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NovaRetail's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Mike Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; David Patel, COO; Lisa Wong, CMO; Raj Singh, CTO; and Emily Zhang, CDO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Thompson, CEO of NovaRetail.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by fulfillment efficiencies and advertising return on ad spend improvements. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with gross merchandise value up 22% year-over-year to $14.2 billion and active customers reaching 45 million.

Our focus remains on mobile app engagement enhancements. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our seasonal strategies, which we believe will significantly mitigate deviations from trends.

We are investing heavily in holiday season inventory optimization.

We are focused on improving seller services adoption.

We are expanding our presence in promotional activity management.

Finally, we are committed to leveraging data for overall operational leverage.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Mike. Our Q3 revenue was $2.9 billion, an increase of 25% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.5%, driven by lower fulfillment costs and scale efficiencies across our logistics network. Operating expenses were $1.0 billion, representing 34.5% of revenue. On marketing spend, we optimized aggressively, achieving a blended ROAS of 5.8x, up significantly year-over-year, which allowed us to drive $1.2 billion in ad-attributed GMV on $207 million in spend—a testament to our channel mix shifts toward high-efficiency platforms like Meta, Google, and emerging retail media networks.

Our net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $0.92 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of $11.5 billion to $12 billion in revenue.

Thank you, Mike. I'll now dive into our fulfillment cost per order, or FCPO, which remains a cornerstone of our operational leverage in this hyper-competitive e-commerce landscape. As you know, FCPO encompasses the full spectrum of our third-party logistics—picking, packing, shipping, last-mile delivery, and returns handling—net of any customer reimbursements. It's a critical lever for margin expansion, especially as we scale against giants like Amazon and Walmart, where fulfillment economics dictate market share in categories from apparel to consumer electronics.

Let me start with the headline numbers for Q3 FY2024. Our FCPO came in at $7.42, down 14% year-over-year from $8.62 in Q3 FY2023, and a sequential improvement of 3% from $7.65 in Q2. This represents our lowest FCPO in three years, driving a 220 basis point expansion in our fulfillment and logistics margin to 12.8% of GMV. On a trailing 12-month basis, FCPO has declined 18% from the peak of $9.05 in Q1 FY2022, when supply chain disruptions from the Omicron wave and Red Sea rerouting inflated ocean freight by 300%. For context, this outperforms the industry benchmark—per our analysis of 25 public e-tailers including Shopify merchants and peers like Wayfair and Chewy—where blended FCPO averaged $8.75 in Q3, per ECDB data.

Visually, if you look at slide 12, you'll see the steady grind lower. From FY2021 to FY2024, FCPO has trended from $9.80 to $7.65 TTM, a compound annual decline of 8%. Key inflection points: Post-2022 normalization, where peak pressures from labor inflation—U.S. warehouse wages up 25% YoY—and fuel costs—diesel at $5.20/gallon—eased as FedEx and UPS volumes stabilized post-pandemic surge. In 2023 acceleration, we lapped easy comps, but more importantly, our initiatives kicked in—FCPO fell 11% YoY as AOV grew 7% to $52, diluting fixed costs. Q3 '24 tailwinds included a sequential dip driven by 22% YoY increase in orders per fulfillment center—throughput now at 1,200 units/hour vs. 980 last year—despite a 15% rise in same-day delivery penetration to 28% of U.S. orders.

That said, headwinds persist: Returns rates ticked up to 22% in apparel—vs. 18% electronics—pressured by TikTok Shop impulse buys, and carrier rate hikes averaged 5.9% for UPS Ground Advantage. Yet, our FCPO as a percentage of revenue held at 18.2%, well below Amazon's reported 25-30% for non-Prime FBA equivalents.

Our edge comes from a $450 million FY2024 capex program—15% of revenue—focused on automation and AI, yielding a 2.8x ROI on a three-year NPV basis. Here's the playbook: We've deployed 1,200 Locus Robotics bots across 45 of our 60 U.S. fulfillment centers, slashing pick times by 42% to 1.9 minutes per order. In our new 500K sq ft mega-DC in Dallas—mirroring Amazon's Shreveport model—robotic arms from Berkshire Grey handle 65% of totes, reducing labor cost per unit by 28% to $2.10. Dwell time for inventory is now under 24 hours, vs. industry 48-hour average.

AI-powered optimization via our proprietary ML demand forecasting engine, integrated with Snowflake and AWS SageMaker, improved accuracy to 92% at the SKU level—up from 84%—cutting overstock safety stock by 19% and emergency air shipments by 35%. Route optimization via partnerships with Onfleet reduced last-mile deadhead miles by 27%, saving $0.18 per package.

We've rolled out 12 urban micro-fulfillment centers in partnership with Alert Innovation's cube-based systems, targeting same-day in top 20 MSAs. This boosted fulfillment velocity for groceries and essentials by 3x. On the carrier side, our volume commitments with USPS—40% of parcels—and DoorDash Drive—15% last-mile—locked in 8-12% discounts vs. spot rates. Launched NovaReturn AI, scanning 85% of returns optically to auto-restock 62%—up from 45%, vs. Shopify's average 50%. This clawed back $0.45 per order in costs.

Regionally: North America—82% of GMV—FCPO at $7.85, best-in-class, thanks to dense FC network—average 50-mile radius to customer. Prime-like NovaFast at 95% on-time beat Amazon's 93% in Q3 per Jungle Scout. Europe—12% of GMV—higher at $8.20 due to stricter ESG regs like EU Packaging Directive and fragmented carriers, but down 16% YoY via localized DCs in Rotterdam and Warsaw. Brexit duties added $0.12/unit, offset by DHL eCommerce deals. APAC/LatAm—6% of GMV—$6.90, our efficiency star—high density in India via Flipkart-inspired model and Brazil MFCs yielded 25% YoY decline, despite rupee volatility.

Fulfillment isn't just a cost center; it's our moat. As GMV scales 22% to $14.2B, fixed automation costs dilute faster than variable shipping—targeting FCPO under $7.00 by FY2025, a 6% further cut. Risks include potential UPS/FedEx labor strikes—10-15% cost upside—and China tariffs on electronics—5% AOV impact—but hedges via diversified sourcing mitigate. We're ahead of the curve versus peers: Wayfair's FCPO rose 4% YoY on housing slowdown, while our 14% drop underscores execution. Looking forward, Q4 guidance embeds $7.25-$7.40 FCPO, with upside from holiday throughput ramps.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we dive into our marketing performance, I'd like to focus on one of our key efficiency metrics: Return on Ad Spend, or ROAS. For those less familiar, ROAS measures the revenue generated for every dollar spent on advertising, calculated as ad-attributed revenue divided by total ad spend. In our high-margin e-commerce model—where we sell everything from fast-fashion apparel and consumer electronics to beauty and home goods—a ROAS above 4x is considered strong, covering our typical 20-25% blended COGS and variable fulfillment costs while delivering healthy contribution margins.

In Q3, we delivered an outstanding blended ROAS of 5.8x, up 28% quarter-over-quarter from 4.5x in Q2 and 15% year-over-year from 5.0x in Q3 last year. This efficiency drove $1.2 billion in ad-attributed gross merchandise value, representing 42% of our total $2.9 billion quarterly GMV, on just $207 million in ad spend—a 12% reduction in absolute spend from Q2 despite 18% GMV growth. Let me break this down by channel, region, and the initiatives fueling these results.

Our performance marketing mix continues to optimize around high-ROAS channels, with a deliberate shift away from broad awareness tactics toward incrementality-tested performance buys. Meta Platforms—Facebook & Instagram—our top performer at 7.2x ROAS, up from 6.1x YoY. Advantage+ Shopping Campaigns and our dynamic product ads leveraging UGC from our 15 million loyalty app users generated 35% of ad-attributed GMV. We've seen a 22% lift from AR try-on features for beauty products, mirroring successes at Sephora and Ulta. However, iOS privacy changes continue to pressure scale, so we're blending server-side API tracking with Meta's Aggregated Event Measurement to maintain 95% attribution accuracy.

Google Ads & YouTube: Steady at 5.4x ROAS, contributing 28% of GMV. Performance Max campaigns, powered by our first-party CRM data via Customer Match, delivered a 19% YoY ROAS uplift. Search ROAS hit 8.1x on high-intent terms like 'wireless earbuds under $50,' but display and YouTube scaled efficiently at 4.2x thanks to our AI-driven video sequencing—short 15-second hooks leading to 6-second shoppable CTAs.

Amazon DSP & Retail Media Networks: A bright spot at 6.9x ROAS, up 35% YoY, driving 22% of GMV. Our offsite DSP buys on Amazon targeted our private-label electronics, achieving 2.5x incrementality per our geo-holdout tests. We're expanding into Walmart Connect and Target Roundel, where early pilots show 5.5x ROAS on CPG categories like our NovaHome kitchenware line. RMNs now represent 18% of spend, with plans to grow to 25% by year-end as closed-loop attribution shines in a cookieless world.

Emerging Channels—TikTok Shop & Pinterest—4.9x ROAS overall, but TikTok Shop exploded to 9.2x on Gen Z fashion drops, accounting for 12% of GMV. Pinterest's dynamic retargeting hit 5.8x for home decor, benefiting from our 40% pinned content from user-generated reviews.

Trend-wise, we've sustained a 20%+ ROAS expansion for five straight quarters, outpacing peers like Etsy—4.2x reported—and Wayfair—3.8x—per Sensor Tower data. This is amid softening CPMs—down 8% YoY industry-wide due to post-iOS 14.5 normalization—but rising CAC competition in apparel from Shein and Temu.

Geographic performance highlights our maturing international flywheel: North America—65% of spend—6.2x ROAS, fueled by US Prime Day synergies—we saw a 45% GMV spike mid-quarter. Canada lagged slightly at 5.1x due to higher logistics costs on cross-border fulfillment. Europe—20% of spend—5.3x ROAS, with strong 7.1x in UK/Germany on Google Shopping after localizing creatives for GDPR compliance. France and Italy improved 18% YoY via TikTok influencer bundles, but regulatory headwinds like the DMA are pushing us toward contextual targeting. APAC—15% of spend—breakout at 4.7x ROAS, up 42% YoY. India scaled to 6.4x on Flipkart alliance ads for budget smartphones, while Southeast Asia—Shopee/Lazada integrations—hit 5.9x via vernacular video ads. China exposure remains minimal at 2% of spend, focused on Tmall Global for premium beauty at 8.2x.

None of this happens without tech. Our proprietary NovaAds platform, built on Google Cloud's Vertex AI and integrated with Snowflake for unified CDP, automates 85% of bidding via multi-touch reinforcement learning models. Key wins: Quarterly geo-experiments showed 28% true uplift from Meta/Amazon spend, allowing us to cut underperforming $15M in Q2. AI A/B testing via Adobe Sensei cycled 1,200 ad variants weekly, boosting CTR 17% and CVR 12%—e.g., personalized 'You left this in your cart' dynamic banners. With third-party cookies phasing out—Google's deadline now mid-2024—70% of our targeting uses first-party data hashed via CAPI and SKAdNetwork 4.0, plus contextual signals from our 2.5 billion annual site sessions. We're piloting Google's PAIR and Topics API for 15% of non-logged-in traffic. Moved to a 7-day click/1-day view data-driven model—vs. Shopify's default last-click—capturing 22% more revenue attribution.

ROAS efficiency is our moat in a commoditizing e-commerce landscape, where Temu's aggressive $1B+ quarterly ad blitz has inflated industry CPMs 15% YoY. We're countering with a 'retail media flywheel': monetizing our 500M+ annual sessions via NovaAds self-serve for brands—Q3 revenue: $28M, up 55%—recycling 40% back into our customer acquisition.

Looking to Q4, we guide to 6.0x+ blended ROAS, targeting $900M+ ad-attributed GMV on flat-to-down spend, assuming stable macro tailwinds like US holiday seasonality. Risks include escalating platform fees—Meta's up 5%—and APAC forex, but our 35% active customer retention and LTV:CAC of 3.8x provide buffer. This discipline not only protects margins—Q3 marketing as % of GMV fell to 7.1% from 8.9% YoY—but funds R&D like AR/VR shopping and same-day drone delivery pilots. We're positioning NovaRetail as the efficiency leader, much like Amazon's ad empire scaled from its logistics dominance.

Thank you, Mike. I'll now dive into the seasonality dynamics that are so core to our business at NovaRetail, the leading omnichannel e-commerce platform specializing in fashion, beauty, and consumer electronics. As you all know, the online retail industry is inherently cyclical, with peaks driven by macroeconomic consumer spending patterns, cultural events, and promotional cadences. Our GMV typically follows a classic bell curve: subdued in Q1 post-holiday normalization, building momentum through back-to-school in Q3, and exploding in Q4 with Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and holiday gifting. Today, I'll break down the FY2024 trends to date, highlight key deviations from our historical baselines and analyst consensus, and share how our technical and strategic levers are smoothing these swings for more predictable growth.

Over the past five years, our seasonality has mirrored broader industry benchmarks from peers like Shopify merchants and Amazon's public filings. Q4 has consistently accounted for 38-42% of annual GMV, fueled by a 4-5x uplift in orders versus Q1 troughs. For context: Q1 average YoY GMV growth of +8%, with AOV dipping to $65 amid post-holiday deleveraging. Traffic volumes drop 25-30% from Q4 peaks as consumers reset budgets. Q2 +15% YoY GMV, driven by Mother's Day, graduations, and early summer promotions. AOV stabilizes at $72. Q3 +25% YoY, propelled by back-to-school campaigns—laptops, apparel, dorm essentials—capturing 22% of annual GMV. Q4 the powerhouse at +45% YoY GMV growth, with Cyber Week alone delivering 15-20% of full-year revenue. AOV spikes to $95+ on gifting bundles.

In FY2024 to date, we're tracking closely, with Q3 GMV up 25% YoY. Q3 performance validated supply chain investments: inventory turnover improved to 8.2x from 7.1x in FY2023, minimizing stockouts to under 2% during peak demand.

While on-trend, we saw targeted deviations earlier: Q1 softness—GMV grew +6% YoY to $3.1B, below +8% historical norm. Culprit? Lingering inflation pressures—U.S. CPI at 3.2% squeezed discretionary spend, echoing Walmart's Q1 comps. CAC rose 11% to $28, driven by higher Google Ads CPCs amid competitive bidding from Shein and Temu. Regionally, hit APAC hardest: China lockdowns residual effects muted Lunar New Year sales by 15% YoY. Q2 acceleration +22% YoY to $4.0B, supercharged by Summer Reset campaign. Deviation explained by early BTS pre-loading and wedding season demand in Europe +35% YoY in UK/DE markets. Our omnichannel playbook—BOPIS fulfillment—drove 28% of Q2 orders, reducing shipping costs 9% and lifting LTV by 14% for hybrid shoppers.

Macro headwinds like FX volatility—USD strength hurt our 25% international GMV—and supply chain snarls from Red Sea disruptions added ~3% drag overall, but our hedging and vendor diversification mitigated to just 1.5% impact.

Regionally: North America—65% of GMV—classic U.S. seasonality intact. Europe—20%—muted Q1 from energy crisis hangovers, but strong Q3 on Boxing Day strength. VAT compliance tech reduced cart abandonment 18%. APAC/LATAM—15%—volatile—India's Diwali drove Q3 +55%, but Brazil's elections caused Q2 dip. We're scaling localized assortments via Shopify Plus integrations.

To derisk swings, three pillars: NovaAI 2.0, our GenAI suite, now predicts demand at SKU-level with 92% accuracy, enabling proactive inventory allocation—early tests show 15% GMV uplift in off-peak quarters. Customer flywheel: Loyalty program revamp targets 30% repeat rate in Q1 from 22%, blending subscriptions with gamified rewards—LTV/CAC now 4.2x. Diversification: Expanding into health/wellness—new category, $500M run-rate—and enterprise B2B via NovaBiz platform, adding 10% recurring revenue less prone to consumer cycles.

Looking forward, we guide FY2024 GMV +20-23%, with Q1 at +10% YoY as inflation eases. Seasonality remains our tailwind, but initiatives turning peaks into plateaus and troughs into ramps.

As we wrap up Q3 results, I'd like to dive deeper into our holiday season preparations, a critical period that historically drives 35-40% of our annual GMV for NovaRetail. With Black Friday through Cyber Monday, followed by the full December ramp-up, we're laser-focused on balancing robust inventory positioning with demand forecasting to capture what we project as a 22% YoY increase in holiday orders.

Heading into the holidays, our ending inventory stands at $1.2 billion, up 18% YoY from $1.02 billion last year, but we've maintained inventory turns at a healthy 8.2x annualized—above our long-term target of 7.5x and in line with top-tier peers like Amazon and Chewy. This build reflects proactive sourcing across our 150,000+ SKUs, with weighted emphasis on high-velocity categories: electronics—42% of inventory value, led by smartphones and smart home devices; apparel—28%, focusing on fast-fashion lines; beauty/home—30%.

Segmented: Safety stock 25% of total, bolstered to cover potential port delays, now at 45 days of inventory on hand vs. industry average of 38 DOH per Deloitte. Promotional stock 35%, pre-positioned for flash sales and bundles, with 60% fulfillment capacity in U.S. and EU DCs. New product intros 15% allocation to trending items like sustainable apparel—up 30% YoY assortment growth—and AI-enhanced wearables.

Sell-through rates from early holiday pre-sales tracking at 92%, validating just-in-time replenishment from Vietnam and Mexico facilities, reduced lead times by 22% via SAP S/4HANA upgrades.

Our demand outlook anchored in proprietary AI/ML model—NovaSense platform, integrating 1.5 petabytes of first-party data, third-party signals from Google Trends and Nielsen, and macro inputs like U.S. consumer confidence at 102—up from 98 YoY. Anticipate holiday GMV of $4.8 billion, 24% increase from $3.9 billion last year, driven by order volume 28 million units +22% YoY, AOV steady at $172, buoyed by cross-sell algorithms boosting bundles by 15%. Category: Electronics +28%; Apparel +19%; Home/Beauty +18%. Traffic: Mobile app sessions up 32% YoY, conversion at 4.8% thanks to hyper-personalized recommendations—dynamic pricing adjusts in real-time for 15% uplift.

Forecast incorporates conservative 5% haircut for inflation persistence and geopolitical risks, but offsets with pent-up demand from Gen Z/Millennials—62% of traffic.

Invested $150 million in CapEx: AI-driven demand sensing—NovaPredict 2.0 using Prophet forecasting with ensemble XGBoost—95% accuracy at SKU-week level, reducing stockouts 40%. Micro-fulfillment centers expanded to 12 U.S. sites, cutting last-mile to under 2 days for 75% orders. Vendor-managed inventory 45% of stock with top suppliers, auto-replenishment based on real-time data. Sustainability: 40% holiday inventory eco-certified, recycled packaging reducing costs 8%.

Regionally: North America—65% holiday GMV—U.S. demand +25%, inventory $780 million. Secured 2x capacity with UPS/FedEx for 15 million parcels. Europe—20%—+18% growth; UK/DE inventory €220 million. Asia-Pacific/LatAm—15%—China Singles' Day proxy +30%; inventory localized. Emerging: Brazil/Mexico +35% on apparel.

Strategically, leaning into endless aisle expansion via Shopify Plus for 5,000+ third-party sellers, projecting 12% GMV lift. BOPIS penetration 22% in Q3. Risks: supply snarls mitigated by dual-sourcing 70% electronics; consumer pullback hedged with dynamic markdowns—12% of promo inventory—and $300 million flexible capital.

Our alignment positions NovaRetail for record holiday, targeting 25-27% full-year revenue growth at 38% adjusted EBITDA margins.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into one of our highest-margin and fastest-growing revenue streams: seller services and value-added services, which collectively generated $2.8 billion in revenue this quarter, up 42% year-over-year and representing 28% of our total net revenue of $10.1 billion. This segment continues to outperform our core marketplace GMV take rate, which grew a solid 18% YoY to $45.2 billion, underscoring the power of our ecosystem strategy in driving sticky, recurring revenue from our 4.2 million active sellers worldwide.

On adoption rates: 68% of active sellers now utilize at least one value-added service, up from 52% a year ago. Fueled by seamless onboarding via Seller Central dashboard and API-first integrations.

Sub-segments: Advertising services—$1.4 billion, 50% of segment—adoption 72% among third-party sellers over $100K GMV, enhanced by NexBoost AI algorithm. Sponsored listings and display ads 15% of total site traffic, CTR improving 28% YoY. Fulfillment via NovaFulfill—$850 million, adoption 45% of eligible—up 15 points YoY; Prime-eligible inventory +55% YoY, boosting marketplace conversion 12%. Payments via NovaPay—processing $28 billion TPV, take rate 2.1%—55% adoption among SMBs, disbursed $1.2 billion loans YTD. Analytics tools—32% adoption, ARPU +65%.

Trends: Q3 launch of Seller Growth Suite—unified API with 1,500 plugins for SAP/NetSuite. $250 million in GenAI, reducing seller churn 22%, cross-sell +18%. Blockchain pilots with 5,000 beta sellers cut fraud 30%.

Regionally: North America $1.1 billion—39% YoY, 75% adoption. APAC $700 million—62% YoY, 82% adoption SEA. EMEA/LATAM $1 billion—45% YoY, LATAM 58%. India challenges but hyperlocal pilots gaining.

Impact: 62% gross margin—double marketplace 11.2%—$1.7 billion contribution profit, 35% of adjusted EBITDA. Flywheel: 2.3x ARPU for engaged sellers, +24% platform GMV halo. Expect 45-50% growth FY2024, 75% adoption.

Seller services transforming NovaRetail into full-stack commerce OS, $12 billion run-rate by year-end.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into one of the key levers we've been actively managing: the impact of our promotional activities on both top-line sales and bottom-line profitability. In the hyper-competitive E-Commerce landscape—Amazon's Prime Day or Alibaba's Singles Day—promotions are table stakes for driving GMV, but executed with precision to avoid margin erosion. In Q3, promotional activity accounted for 28% of our $14.2 billion GMV, up from 22% last year.

Sales acceleration: Aggressive calendar anchored by Flash Fest, delivering 32% YoY lift, contributing to 25% revenue growth. High-velocity categories—electronics, fashion 55% GMV—AOV $85 during promos vs. $92 non-promo, volume +45%. Beauty 52% GMV spike from bundles, 1.2 million new customers. Cross-sell 42% of promo buyers added upsells, basket +15%. CAC $18 new user—down 12% YoY—targeted campaigns open rates 38%. Retention 65% within 30 days, LTV $450/24 months, LTV:CAC 4.2x.

Regionally: North America 48% GMV, Black Friday 28% lift. Europe 25% GMV, 22% uplift localized. APAC 30% GMV 41% on Singles Day equivalents, UPI integrations abandonment -22%. LATAM 15% YoY bump.

Profitability: Gross margins compressed 320 bps to 41.2% from 44.4%, average discount 18%. Fulfillment % GMV 14.5%, mitigated by vendor-funded 35% discounts. Contribution 22% promo vs. 28% steady-state, but volume pushed EBITDA +14% to $420 million. ROAS promo media 5.8x, AI dynamic pricing optimized 70% deals. Inventory turns 8.2x.

Evolving: PromoGenix ML platform segments 250 micro-cohorts, +25% conversion, -10% dilution. OmniRewards 2.0 exclusive boosts, 40% promo to high-LTV. BOPIS 35% promo traffic, logistics -18%. Eco promos +55%.

Expect mid-teens GMV growth FY24, margins 42-43%, balancing share gains.

Now I'll turn it over to David Patel to discuss operations.

David Patel:
Thanks, Sarah. Operationally, we focused on scaling fulfillment throughput and last-mile velocity. Our shipping times improved by 25% to an average of 1.8 days. Fulfillment costs were down 14% per order. We are implementing advanced robotics and AI route optimization across our network, aligning with the FCPO improvements Sarah detailed.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa Wong.

Lisa Wong:
Thanks, David. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Advantage+ campaigns on Meta and Performance Max on Google, reinforcing the 5.8x ROAS Sarah highlighted. Customer acquisition costs were $22, down from prior quarters. Our brand awareness increased by 18%. We are focusing on retail media expansion and privacy-first targeting for sustained efficiency.

Now I'll turn it over to Raj Singh.

Raj Singh:
Thanks, Lisa. On the technology front, we've been focused on app infrastructure upgrades and AI personalization. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 22% to 28 million MAU. Thank you, and good afternoon, everyone. This is Raj Singh, but with Sarah's lead on metrics, let me reinforce: mobile continues as growth engine, 62% of GMV—up from 55% YoY—outpacing desktop 3:1. Record 4.8 million new downloads, 28% YoY, iOS 55%. Total lifetime 185 million. ShopSwift referral +15% organic. Ahead of Etsy, chasing Shein.

Active users: MAU 28 million +22% YoY, DAU 12.5 million—45% ratio top-tier. D30 retention 42% via ML pushes 3x open rates. Session length 6.2 min +18%, in-app live-stream. Cohorts strong, exceeds Walmart benchmarks.

Conversion 5.2% +15% YoY, outpaces web. One-tap checkout abandonment 22%. AOV $68 +14%. App GMV $1.2B 45% total, ROAS 4.2x.

Trends: iOS attribution stabilized SKAdNetwork 4.0 85% match. App-first exclusives, StyleMatch GenAI +28% fashion. Web3 NFTs +20% LTV. Flutter migration -40% dev. Q4 AR/VR Meta Llama 10-15% uplift.

Regions: NA 55% GMV 15M MAU 6.8% conv. Europe 20% 6M 4.9%. APAC 18% 8M 5.8%. LatAm/MENA 7% 4.5%.

LTV 2.5x web $450/12 mo, CAC $12. Guide 25% app GMV growth, 35M MAU 6%+ conv.

We're investing in edge computing for faster app experiences.

Now I'll turn it over to Emily Zhang.

Emily Zhang:
Thanks, Raj. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 15% improvement in conversion rates because of our AI demand forecasting. We are also focusing on privacy enhancements with first-party data strategies.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Mike, can you expand on how seasonality deviations impacted your guidance and macro outlook?

Mike Thompson:
Thanks, John. As Sarah detailed extensively, our seasonality tracked closely with historical bell curves, but Q1 softness from inflation was offset by Q2 and Q3 accelerations via omnichannel and BTS surges. We've smoothed swings with NovaAI at 92% accuracy and loyalty revamps, reaffirming full-year guide with confidence in resilient consumer trends.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley.

Maria Lopez:
Great, thanks. Sarah, could you elaborate on FCPO trends and how holiday prep factors into Q4 margins?

Sarah Chen:
Absolutely, Maria. As I covered, FCPO at $7.42 down 14% YoY, driven by robotics scaling to 1,200 bots, AI forecasting 92% accurate, and micro-FCs. Holiday inventory $1.2B at 8.2x turns, demand sensing for $4.8B GMV—margins supported by VMI 45% and BOPIS synergies, targeting sub-$7.00 FCPO FY25.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan.

David Kim:
Thanks. David, on ops, how are you ensuring fulfillment scales for holiday demand without cost spikes?

David Patel:
Good question, David. Building on Sarah's FCPO playbook, we're ramping throughput to 1,200 units/hour, NovaFast 95% on-time, with DoorDash/USPS discounts and returns AI restocking 62%. 12 MFCs cover 75% same-day metro, hedged for surges.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Patel with Barclays.

Priya Patel:
Congrats team. Lisa, on ROAS—how sustainable is 5.8x amid competition, and promo tie-in?

Lisa Wong:
Thanks, Priya. Sarah's deep dive nailed it—Meta 7.2x, RMNs 6.9x, NovaAds AI automating 85% bidding. Promos amplified with 32% sales lift at 5.8x ROAS, vendor-funded minimizing dilution, LTV:CAC 3.8x buffer vs. Temu pressure.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Chen with Citi.

Alex Chen:
